- When sentiment turns negative for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecasted price by 2–5% to account for bearish momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model tends to overcorrect; cap forecast decline at 3–4% below peak to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +1, -1, +1), model often misreads trend direction; favor mean-reversion bias toward 3–5 day average.  
- In 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong downward trend (e.g., >3 consecutive drops), model often underestimates depth; add 1–2% buffer below forecast to account for lag.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., 7+ days of +1), model tends to overestimate upside; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high to avoid overbought bias.
